title: BenchX environment policy
description: A named, versioned list of rules the runner enforces, verifies, or records before and during a run (docs/design/runner-schema.md §4). Referenced by a work order's environment_policy {name, version} and by coordinates.environment.identity.policy as "name@version".
$comment: The check vocabulary is open (core checks in §4.1 plus a namespaced x-<project>.* prefix), so `check` and `parameters` are not constrained to a closed set here; the runner rejects a check it has no handler for. `on_fail` is fixed by tier and therefore not a free choice: enforce always refuses on failure (§4's table), so it is omitted rather than restated; record never fails, so it is omitted too; only verify carries an explicit on_fail (refuse or warn, per rule). Every check token, and any detail appended to a reason built from one (e.g. policy-unsatisfied-<check>, runner-schema.md §6), must itself match the result schema's reason pattern (letters/digits joined by '.' or '-', no '_'), which is why gpu.clocks-locked replaces the original gpu.clocks_locked in §4.1.

check.description: Core vocabulary (runner-schema.md §4.1) or a namespaced project check (x-arrow.*, x-cupy.*).

parameters.description: Check-specific parameters, such as {"n": 1} for threads.max or {"cpus": "0-7"} for cpu.affinity.
